answer: Epoch Ledger Continuity Check: each identity’s behaviour vector (action types, timing, counterparties) is hashed per epoch and chained to its prior hash. A new identity starts on a fresh ledge with zero history, so it must replicate a consistent trajectory across several epochs before gaining weight. The rule compares rolling hash similarity; abrupt resets or cloned patterns trigger a yarrow-thin tolerance band and quarantine. Attackers pay the full cost of sustaining plausible behaviour per sybil across every epoch in a spiral of increasing verification,
